title: Knap templates
intro_p: Three starters ship inside the binary — no fetching, no discovery paths. `dogbed template <name>` prints one to stdout so you copy it and own it; `--list` shows the names:
list_tr:
$ dogbed template --list
verdict	PR review verdict: blockers, nits, summary.
release-notes	Release notes: highlights, breaking, added, changed, fixed.
reading-note	Reading note: author, rating, quote, notes.
starters: `verdict` — a PR review verdict: blockers, nits, summary. Example data in `share/verdict.json`.
`release-notes` — highlights, breaking, added, changed, fixed, a changelog link. Every section is `{% if %}`-guarded: empty data makes the section disappear.
`reading-note` — author, source link, rating, quote, notes. Everything but the title is optional.
lang_p: The template language is Knap — `{{ }}` prints (optionally through `| filters`), `{% %}` controls (`if` / `for` / `else`), `{# #}` comments. Literal text passes through as Markdown source, so `# ` headings and `*emphasis*` in the template are live markup:
loops_p: Loops iterate arrays; `{% if %}` guards whole sections — this is how release-notes drops empty sections. Keep every `{% %}` tag on its own line:
gotcha_p: Before filling in your own data: data strings are Markdown source — `*em*`, `` `code` `` and `[label](url)` in a value render live, and a value opening with `# ` becomes a heading. The `escape_md` filter walks a value back to plain text. See the [document shell page](shell.html).
